question: It is of great concern that, in the USA, avian influenza A has been detected not just on poultry farms but also in the dairy sector – in raw milk, milking equipment, slurry and even in the air on farms – and there is a high risk that after crossing into cattle it will mutate and appear in humans. 1.
What measures is the Commission taking to strengthen surveillance and biosecurity systems on European farms so as to prevent a similar scenario arising in the European Union?
Does the Commission intend to develop further guidance for Member States on monitoring in the dairy sector, including the systematic analysis of raw milk and of dairy farm environments?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.10.2025) 1. In April 2025, the Commission issued guidance1 on measures the EU may apply under different Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) scenarios, including surveillance, reporting and control measures.

In addition, the European Food Safety Authority provided scientific and technical assistance2 on the risk posed by the HPAI virus currently circulating in the United States and further advice is expected by November 2025. 2. The aforementioned guidance may be updated, if needed, depending on the evolution of the situation and scientific advice made available.
